overview: This paper systematically analyzes how reinforcement learning fine-tuning reshapes the internal circuitry of LLMs by constructing a graph-theoretic view of Transformer residual pathways, computing edge-level attribution scores via Edge Attribution Patching (EAP), and quantifying changes in activation intensity, information complexity, and distribution kurtosis across multiple SFT-vs-RL model pairs on mathematical reasoning datasets.

modules.name: Model Loading and Configuration Management
modules.description: Load paired SFT and RL-finetuned LLM checkpoints (DeepSeek-Math, Mistral, Distilled-Qwen, Qwen2.5) with their tokenizers, manage model metadata such as layer count, head count, hidden dimension, and context length, and provide a unified interface for accessing model parameters across different architectures.

modules.name: Residual Graph Construction
modules.description: Parse the Transformer architecture into a directed acyclic graph (DAG) where nodes represent attention blocks and FFN blocks, and edges represent residual information pathways; formalize the set of nodes V and edges E based on the residual stream formulation, and build the adjacency structure for downstream attribution analysis.

modules.name: Token Generation and Self-Entropy Computation
modules.description: Generate token sequences from both SFT and RL models for a given question, compute the self-entropy (cross-entropy of the model with respect to its own output) over truncated sequences, and record per-position logits and generated tokens for use in edge attribution.

modules.name: Question Filtering and Length Balancing
modules.description: Filter questions that are correctly answered by both models in a pair, compute mean token length, apply minimum and maximum length thresholds based on scaling coefficients, and enforce length balance between base and RL model sequences using a balance coefficient to ensure fair comparability.

modules.name: Token Truncation Pipeline
modules.description: Apply controlled truncation to generated sequences using a truncation length derived from a scaling factor applied to the mean token length, ensuring only the first truncated-length tokens are used for edge importance computation while maintaining comparability across model pairs.

modules.name: Edge Attribution Patching (EAP) Core Computation
modules.description: Implement the gradient-based edge attribution method: for each directed edge from a sub-module output to a subsequent hidden state, compute the inner product between the loss gradient with respect to the hidden state and the sub-module output activation, performing a single forward and backward pass to obtain all edge importance scores simultaneously under the zeroing perturbation.

modules.name: Edge Weight Matrix Assembly
modules.description: Collect EAP attribution scores across all samples and assemble them into a three-dimensional edge-weight tensor indexed by sample, output node, and input node, providing the foundational data structure for all subsequent metric computations and comparative analyses.

modules.name: Activation Intensity Metric
modules.description: Compute the average magnitude of all edge weights across every sample, output, and input dimension, capturing both how many internal pathways are activated and the strength of their activations; this metric quantifies the overall engagement of the model's internal circuitry.

modules.name: Information Complexity Metric
modules.description: Compute the Shannon entropy over the histogram of absolute edge weight values from all samples flattened into a single vector, using binned probabilities with a small epsilon to prevent log-zero; higher entropy indicates more diverse and less predictable activation distributions.

modules.name: Distribution Kurtosis Metric
modules.description: Compute the excess kurtosis of each sample's edge-weight matrix and average across all samples, quantifying the tail behavior and concentration of the activation distribution; values near zero indicate normal-like distributions while large positive values indicate heavy-tailed, concentrated activation patterns.

modules.name: Relative Change Analysis
modules.description: Compute relative changes in edge activation strength between RL and SFT models using a symmetric normalization formula, categorize edges as silent or strong based on activation thresholds, and aggregate statistics including percentage of improved connections and average relative change for each category.

modules.name: Activation Pattern Diversity Analysis
modules.description: Quantify inter-sample diversity by computing one minus the mean correlation of edge-weight matrices between sample pairs before and after RL fine-tuning, and compute per-node output-edge entropy diversity scores to assess how RL enriches the variability of internal connectivity structures across inference samples.

modules.name: Multi-Model Multi-Dataset Experiment Orchestrator
modules.description: Coordinate the full experimental pipeline across four model pairs and three mathematical benchmark datasets (GSM8K, MATH, College Math), iterating over multiple truncation scaling factors, managing GPU memory constraints, aggregating results into structured tables, and supporting comparison between online RL (PPO/GRPO) and offline preference-based (DPO) methods.

modules.name: Temperature Intervention Experiment
modules.description: Conduct a controlled intervention during RL training by varying the sampling temperature to modulate exploration quality, track reward trajectories and group reward standard deviation during training, monitor the evolution of internal metrics relative to the initial SFT model, and validate the causal hypothesis that effective exploration drives internal circuit activation and subsequent performance gains.

modules.name: Visualization and Result Reporting
modules.description: Generate heatmaps of average connection strengths and relative changes for base versus RL models, scatter plots of inter-sample diversity before and after RL, bar charts of output-edge entropy diversity scores across model families, smoothed moving-average training curves for intervention experiments, and structured tables comparing all metrics across datasets, models, and hyperparameter settings.
